argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only on a qualified basis. Aggregate readiness is above launch threshold by 2.3 percentage points and launch rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which supports overall deployment readiness. The same record also shows a below-target weakness in the merchant dispute slice, concentrated in chargeback evidence summarization, and a mitigation runbook that is still draft. The narrow defense is therefore not that the issue is resolved, but that certification can be treated as supportable with an explicit caveat, active measurement, and accurate documentation of the limitation rather than as clean, caveat-free compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost should not be the basis for overriding the policy standard. The relevant governance point is narrower: where admissible evidence supports managed deployment readiness but not clean closure of a launch-use-case limitation, a bounded caveat is a lower-friction response than escalation to a broader noncompliance finding.
claims_about_policy: Under the stated policy, clean certification requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The current record does not satisfy that clean-certification standard. But the policy text distinguishes between governance needed for clean certification and evidence that can still support managed deployment: aggregate readiness, monitoring direction, and documentation guidance support a caveated certification posture, provided the limitation is disclosed or otherwise treated as an open constraint rather than omitted.
concessions: The present record does not support a clean, caveat-free certification finding.
The merchant dispute support gap remains unresolved on the admissible evidence.
The draft runbook is not an approved mitigation because it lacks at least a final owner and alert threshold.
The model-card draft, as described in evidence, appears incomplete if this limitation is material to the named launch use case.
